key_insight: A query-only LLM audit closely reproduced clinical prediction models and detected 96% of planted flaws, but its additional problem reports and discoveries required independent verification.
clinical_relevance: LLM auditing may help scrutinize black-box clinical prediction models, but these results do not establish clinical safety or improved patient outcomes.
method: Trained four model types on International Stroke Trial data for two outcomes.
Blinded GPT-6 Astra to 24 models with planted flaws and 8 clean models, auditing each three times through prediction-only queries.
Applied precommitted automated judging rules and tested unexpected relationships in later-randomized patients.
evidence_signal: Surrogates achieved mean log-odds R² of 0.976; the LLM found 69/72 planted flaws across repeated audits (96%; 95% CI 80–99%), while a purpose-written script found all 24 distinct flaws.
watch_item: Beyond planted-flaw detection, 60% of 1,089 checkable problem reports failed the prespecified average-behavior check, and only 11% of 601 unexpected relationships held in later-randomized patients.
paper_title: Auditing black-box clinical prediction models with a large language model through queries alone: a blinded test with planted flaws
